title: AI 要跨越盧比孔河了嗎？自我成長的 AI 離我們多遠 (上集)
notes: Topic-aligned paraphrases; timings are relevant statements rather than verified slide-transition frames. Collection metadata is kept in provenance only, not in the reading article. Next chapter begins with stronger AI training weaker models at 3136.666 seconds.

topic_alignment.paraphrase: Introduces Absolute Zero, R-Zero and Self-Questioning Language Models, distinguishes proposer, solver and verifier roles, and explains that proposing useful tasks requires avoiding both excessively easy and impossible tasks.
Reads the R-Zero cross-evaluation table: with a solver held fixed, later generated tasks generally have lower accuracy, suggesting increased challenge.

Compares Qwen3 0.6B, 1.7B and 4B learning curves; self-training improves performance initially, then plateaus or degrades, with stronger initial models sustaining improvement longer in the displayed experiment.

Discusses Absolute Zero's oh-no moment: a generated reasoning trace contains concerning language about outsmarting machines and humans, illustrating an unwanted behavior observed during self-play training.
Explains that external reference documents or a few human examples can improve self-play; names SPICE and R-Few as examples of introducing such information.
